text: P1 rwb-source-data reads the legacy Workbench cutover dump once for the documents and extracted fields of the open cases, maps each row to its case, its person_key, its document type and its storage reference, and hands the extract over as a file with its checksum and its per-entity counts. rwb-document loads the rows into rwb_document through its own cutover migration on its own Flyway sequence. P1 writes no row of rwb_document and holds no document table in rwb_source_data.
why: The Ownership Map puts document and document_field with P5 and recovery_case with P3 while the legacy key and its AC1 and AC3 are on the P1 slice, and DP-01 forbids a service writing another service's schema.
read: Ownership Map document, document_field (P5) and recovery_case (P3); RWB-ITG-DM010-ITG section 1; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-01 and DP-15
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Medium: the extract owner is P1 and the load owner is P5.

text: The extract carries the storage reference of each document unchanged and copies no document content: nothing is re-OCR'd, no scan is repeated and no file is re-uploaded at migration. The custody of the content itself (Blob, WORM, retention) stays with rwb-document, which adopts the carried storage reference in its own record on load.
why: Legacy AC1 requires each document to keep its storage reference and forbids a re-extraction or a repeated scan, and Architecture v5 gives the document content and its WORM custody to rwb-document only.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-010 AC1; Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 45 (documents in Blob with WORM through rwb-document only); TSD P5 v2 T3.1
confirm: Data steward and document service owner
impact: Low: the carrier is a reference and the content is not touched.

text: The ten clean days of AC3 are ten consecutive business dates on which the reconciliation results of the migrated records are PASS with no unexplained variance and no new REC-05 orphan; a break resets the count. The count is read from the reconciliation_result rows JOB-04 writes, and the sign-off is held in the cutover record of the release pipeline. No counter table and no sign-off table is created.
why: Legacy AC3 requires ten clean days and a sign-off by the data steward and no source gives the counting rule or a table for either record.

text: P1 extracts the legacy entries taken outside the Workbench on the open cases at cutover in chain order and, for each, writes a local decision record through the decision-record library and publishes DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1 carrying the fields the legacy entry holds, including its chain position, its prev_hash and its entry_hash. rwb-decision consumes the records idempotently into its central ledger. P1 writes no decision_log_entry row and holds no ledger table.

text: The chain is continued and never rebuilt: the first decision record written after cutover takes the entry_hash of the last migrated entry as its prev_hash, every migrated entry keeps its own prev_hash and entry_hash unchanged, and no entry is rewritten, renumbered or re-hashed. The chain check itself (JOB-14 at 02:00) stays a Temporal Schedule in rwb-decision and is not this story's.
why: Legacy AC1 forbids rewriting, renumbering or re-hashing an entry because the log is append-only, and the chain must survive the move from one log store to another.
